method: python training/confirm_tv_blend.py --amazon-dir amazon-movies-tv The first attempt (training/confirm_tv.py) tied with "most popular shows": on Amazon most people rate only a few shows, mostly the same big ones. A blend of the two is the standard answer to a strong popularity baseline, so this is one more try, decided by a rule written before running. Same data, same show/movie matching, same item-kNN. A fresh random group of people (different from the first attempt) with at least 3 loved movies and 2 loved shows is held out entirely; similarities come only from everyone else. Each held-out person's loved movies rank every show by (1 - a) * fans-like-you percentile + a * popularity percentile. - a is picked from 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8 on one half of the held-out people, by NDCG@20. - On the other half, with a fixed, it ships only if it beats "most popular shows" with a   paired-bootstrap 95% interval above zero. This is the last attempt with this data: if it fails, TV stays on "coming next" in the README. If it ships, data/tv_knn.npz is built from everyone, with the blend weight. Writes data/tv_blend_confirm.json.
